hypothesis: Source-anchored bounded mean correction can reduce observation-offset bias while limiting movement-mixture harm
bounded: same EMA state; prediction subtracts clip(previous_m, -cap*training_sd, cap*training_sd)
initial_correction: zero at every provider file or diagnostic window

observation_offset.intervention: Add positive 0.5 * training filtered channel SD to every raw channel/bin for the complete file, before causal filtering
observation_offset.representation: synthetic nonnegative real-valued counts; not a biological acquisition model
observation_offset.filter_startup: zero raw history at file reset; added offset ramps through the existing FIR

movement_mixture.selection: Select one contiguous 3000-bin interval per file maximizing signed unmasked mean target[:,6]; ties choose earliest start
movement_mixture.selection_role: retrospective evaluator-only diagnostic; selection labels never enter the predictor
movement_mixture.length_requirement: every development evaluation file must have at least 3000 bins or the run fails
movement_mixture.state: reset at the start of each selected window; retain original rows and mask; no stitching or history pre-roll
movement_mixture.interpretation: a label-selected movement-mixture stress with fresh-start state, not real cross-session evidence

decision.offset_benefit: positive mean R2 difference versus frozen on offset condition
decision.mixture_guard: strictly smaller worst-day R2 harm versus frozen than ordinary EMA; harm floored at zero
decision.tie_break: largest real mean R2 gain, then smaller cap
decision.fallback: retain frozen normalization; no additional parameter search

randomness: none; fixed weights and deterministic streaming arithmetic
scoring: per-condition day grouping/mask; equal-day mean variance-weighted R2; report every output/day, harm count/fraction, worst harm, residual bias decomposition
